title: How to play
intro:
**Indonesia: How to play**

A guided game against the Sultan of Solo and the businessman from North Sumatra: three years, two eras, every rule. About half an hour.

steps.welcome: Indonesia is a game about getting rich. Whoever has the most money at the end of the game wins. You'll learn it by playing the first three years of a game against two rivals, and by the end you'll have seen every rule. I'll explain each piece as it comes up.
steps.goal: Money is counted in rupiah, and you keep yours in two places, shown here on your mat. Cash is what you spend: you start with 100. The Bank is money put away for good: you can't spend it, but it still counts at the end. You'll see how money gets there soon. In this lesson everyone's money is out in the open; in a normal game it's secret, and you see only your own until the game ends.
steps.whole-game: You get rich by starting companies. Some grow goods, like rice. Others own ships, and carry those goods to the cities that buy them. Every sale pays someone. The rest you'll pick up as we go.
steps.map: Everything you build goes on this map of the islands. Cities and plantations stand on land, in the areas marked out inside each province; ships sail the seas, which blue lines divide. Here and there a little arrow joins two pieces of land across the water: when a plantation grows, they count as neighbours. You'll start here, in Jawa Barat, on the island of Java.
steps.year: The game is played in years, and every year runs through the same seven phases: 1) new cities, 2) bidding for the order of play, 3) mergers, 4) starting companies, 5) research, 6) running your companies, 7) cities growing. You don't need to remember them: they're in the player aid, up here, which always shows the year and the phase. We'll take them one at a time.
steps.city-cards: Phase one: new cities. Cities are where goods get sold, so where they stand matters. You hold three city cards, tucked under your mat. Each card names three provinces; when its era comes, you build a city in one of them. The game has three eras, A, B and C, each lasting a few years, and you hold one card for each. What ends an era, you'll see in year three. Era A starts now.
steps.others-sultan-city: Your two rivals build first. First, the Sultan of Solo. The card turns face up: Jawa Tengah, Sulawesi Utara, Bali. And the city goes in Bali.
steps.others-sumatran-city: Next, the businessman from North Sumatra, the Sumatran for short. The card: Sumatera Selatan, Sulawesi Selatan, Jawa Timur. And a city in Sumatera Selatan.
steps.your-card: Your turn. Your era A card names Jawa Barat, Bali and Jawa Timur. Bali already has a city, and a province may only ever hold one.
steps.build-city: Build yours in Jawa Barat: tap this area on the north coast. A city must stand on the coast, where ships can reach it, in an empty area.
steps.city-built: There it is: a city, size one, the smallest. Every year a city buys goods: one of each kind of good being grown anywhere on the map. A bigger city buys more of each. Keep an eye on this one.
steps.confirm-city: When you finish a turn, the game asks you to confirm it. Until you do, you can still take your move back with Undo. Tap Confirm.
steps.order: Phase two: the order of play. These discs show who goes first in everything that follows this year. The order starts at random, and you are last. Going last means choosing last: the best companies may be gone before your turn comes.
steps.bid-explain: So everyone bids rupiah to go earlier, up to the cash they have, one at a time, in the old order. Highest bid goes first, and a tie keeps the old order. Here's the trick. A bid isn't lost. It goes into your Bank, which still counts at the end. All it costs you is cash you can no longer spend.
steps.others-sumatran-bid: The Sumatran bids ten, and will go first.
steps.bid-up: Bid five, to go ahead of the Sultan: tap plus five.
steps.bid-confirm: And confirm your bid of five.
steps.new-order: The Sumatran first, then you, then the Sultan. Look at your money: five has moved from your cash into your Bank. You're no poorer. You just can't spend it.
steps.no-mergers: Phase three: mergers, where two companies become one. Nobody can merge yet. It takes research, and nobody has done any. Remember that. It will be your move before long.
steps.companies: Phase four: starting companies. These are the companies you can start this era. Each card is a company's deed: it says where the company is, and what it does, grow a good or run ships. Its round marker on the map shows where it will begin.
steps.symbols: The map already tells you which companies and cities each era will bring. Beside every province's name are three groups of symbols, for eras A, B and C, split by slashes. A hut means a city card of that era names the province; a good's symbol, or a ship, means a company of that era starts there. Jawa Barat's say: in era A, a city and rice; in era B, a city and a shipping line; in era C, a city. So you can plan years ahead.
steps.slots: Starting a company costs nothing. The limit is room. You can only own as many companies as you have slots, and everyone starts with just one. Research brings more; we'll come to research shortly.
steps.others-sumatran-company: The Sumatran goes first, and starts the Lampung shipping line. A shipping company owns ships, not land. Its first ship goes into a sea beside its province: this one, between Lampung and Jawa Barat. Look at the Lampung deed: its numbers say how many ships the line may have in each era: two in era A, three in B, four in C.
steps.pick-company: Each kind of good sells at its own price: rice for 20 rupiah, spice for 25, and the later goods for more. Start with rice: Jawa Barat rice. Tap its marker, off the coast of Jawa Barat.
steps.place-plantation: A rice company starts with one plantation: a rice marker on an empty land area in its province. Plant it here, on the coast where the Sumatran's ship is. One rule for later: a plantation may never touch another company's plantation of the same good. You'll see why that matters in era B.
steps.plantation-placed: Your first plantation, with your hut on it to show it's yours. And the deed has moved to your mat: you own a company.
steps.confirm-company: Confirm, and the Sultan takes a turn.
steps.others-sultan-company: The Sultan starts the other rice company: Bali rice, beside the Sultan's own city.
steps.research: Phase five: research. Every year, each player gets better at one thing, for free, by moving one cube one step along these tracks. Each track improves something different, and I'll explain each one when it matters. A track has five steps, and a cube at the end goes no further.
steps.others-sumatran-research: The Sumatran goes first, and takes Slots: room for a second company.
steps.research-mergers: Your turn. You want Mergers. Two companies can only merge once your Mergers cube reaches step two, and that Bali rice is worth watching. Tap the next step on the Mergers row.
steps.operations: Phase six: running the companies. In the order of play, each player runs one company, then the next player, round and round until every company has run once. You choose which of your companies runs, and you must run one each time, even when it can do nothing useful.
steps.others-sumatran-operate: The Sumatran goes first, with the shipping line. A shipping company doesn't sell anything itself: it adds a ship, or more with Expansion research, each next to one it already has. This one goes beside your city. That's two, the most the Lampung deed allows in era A. A line's money comes from carrying other people's goods.
steps.operate-rice: Your turn. Tap your plantation to run Jawa Barat rice. A company's pieces lift off the map while it runs, so everyone can see which one it is.
steps.selling: Running a rice company means selling its rice. Goods never travel over land, not even next door. They leave by ship, and can ride a chain of ships from one sea into the next, as long as every ship belongs to the same company. The chain starts in a sea that touches the plantation, and ends in a sea that touches a city. Here: from your plantation, onto the Sumatran's first ship, onto the second, and to your city.
steps.sell: Tap your city to sell it your rice.
steps.display: Your rice rode both of the Sumatran's ships to your city, and landed on the card that came out of it: the city's goods display. It has a circle for each size of the city, and each circle holds one of each good. So what the city still buys this year is whatever its circles still lack.
steps.sold: Look at the ships' round markers: they flipped over. A ship carries one good for each company each year, and its markers turn back when that company's run is over. Rice sells for 20 rupiah, and every ship it rides charges 5: two ships, 10 to the Sumatran. That leaves you 10, kept apart as this year's earnings until the year ends.
steps.forced: Would you rather not pay a rival? Too bad. Selling isn't a choice: a company must sell as many goods as it can, every time it runs, even when the fees eat the whole price. If they eat more than that, the loss comes out of this year's earnings. When there are several ways to sell, you pick which city, and whose ships. The cheapest isn't always best: you might pay 15 to a player who's behind rather than 10 to the leader. You just can't sell less.
steps.free-expansion: You sold every good your company has. A company that does that grows, for free: it must take new areas of land, each empty and touching one of its plantations, across a province border if need be, or joined to one by an arrow. How many is your Expansion research: one, for now.
steps.expand: Tap this area, next to your first plantation.
steps.expanded: Two plantations now, and this one touches the ship beside your city.
steps.confirm-operate: Your deed has turned face down: that company is done for the year. Confirm, and the Sultan runs Bali rice.
steps.others-sultan-operate: The Sultan runs Bali rice. No ship touches it, so it sells nothing. A plantation with no ship nearby earns nothing at all.
steps.growth: Phase seven: cities grow. A city that got one of every good grown anywhere on the map grows a size. Rice is the only good grown so far, and your city got its rice. So it grows to size two: from now on it buys two of each good, and its display will come out with two circles. Then the goods on every display go into their city, and the displays after them, ready for next year. City markers are limited, and when a size runs out, no more cities can grow into it; if too few are left for the cities that earned one, the first player in the order chooses.
steps.year-2: A new year, and your 10 rupiah of earnings become cash. No new cities: those come only with a new era. An era ends when the companies on offer run out, or when every one left is the same kind. Era A still offers spice and shipping, so it goes on.
steps.others-sumatran-bid-2: Bidding goes in last year's order. One research track, the top one, multiplies bids: at its second step each rupiah counts five, then 25, 100 and 400, and whoever has it must use it. Nobody has it yet. The Sumatran bids nothing.
steps.bid-2: Your turn. A tie keeps last year's order, so nothing keeps you ahead of the Sultan: bid nothing.
steps.others-sultan-bid-2: The Sultan bids nothing too, and the order stays.
steps.mergers-now: Phase three: mergers. And this time you can. Your Mergers cube is on step two, so you may merge two companies of the same good, or two shipping lines, as long as the result holds no more than two deeds. Each step of Mergers allows one deed more.
steps.merger-why: Jawa Barat rice and Bali rice, merged, are one company with three plantations, and the only rice company on the map. Every rice sold to the cities would be yours.
steps.announce: Announce it on the map: tap one of your rice plantations.
steps.announce-second: Then tap the Sultan's plantation in Bali.
steps.merger-table: Here's the deal, laid out on the table. A merger is sold at auction. The two owners may bid, and so may anyone with a free slot. Bidding opens at what the companies are worth, 20 rupiah a plantation, so 60, and each raise adds one rupiah per plantation.
steps.payout: Whoever wins pays the bid to the two owners, split by plantations: two parts to you, one part to the Sultan. So part of what you pay comes straight back to you.
steps.open-bid: You announced it, so you open the bidding: tap Bid 60.
steps.confirm-open: Confirm, and the bidding passes to the Sultan.
steps.others-sultan-raises: The Sultan isn't letting Bali go cheaply: 63.
steps.others-sumatran-passes: The Sumatran researched Slots, so has a free slot, and may bid too. Not interested: a pass, and a player who passes is out of this auction.
steps.raise: Raise to 66. You may bid only cash you have, all of it, even the part that would come back to you.
steps.confirm-raise: Confirm, and it's the Sultan's turn to answer.
steps.won: It's yours. You paid 66, and 44 of it came straight back to you, 22 to the Sultan. The Bali deed sits under yours on your mat: one company now, taking just one slot. And the Bali plantation carries your hut.
steps.merger-rules: A few more things about mergers. Players take turns announcing them, round after round, until nobody wants another, and a company can merge only once a year. Anyone with the research may announce a merger with your company in it, if they own the other company or have a free slot. So keep some cash in hand: it's how you defend what you own. And when two shipping lines merge, their ship limits add up.
steps.acquisitions-2: Phase four again. Your one slot is full, so you sit this out. Players take one company per round, round after round, until everyone has passed or nothing is left; a player who passes is done for the year.
steps.others-sumatran-spice: The Sumatran has a free slot, and starts Halmahera spice, far to the east.
steps.others-sultan-spice: The Sultan starts Maluku spice, close by, then passes.
steps.spice-now: Now spice is grown on the map. So from now on every city wants spice as well as rice, as many of each as its size, and must get all of it to grow. What a city wants is whatever is being grown anywhere, right now.
steps.others-sumatran-hull: Research. The Sumatran takes Hull. Hull is how many goods a ship carries for each company: from now on, each Sumatran ship can carry two of yours. You can even move another player's Hull cube instead of your own, if their ships carry your goods.
steps.research-mergers-3: Take Mergers again, to step three. Next year a new kind of merger becomes possible, and it will need three deeds. More on that then. Tap the next step on the Mergers row.
steps.lampung-full: Phase six. The Lampung line has nothing to do: it already has two ships, its limit for era A. A company with nothing it could do is run for you.
steps.others-sumatran-spice-run: The Sumatran runs Halmahera spice. No ship anywhere near it: nothing sold.
steps.operate-rice-2: Your turn. Run your rice company: tap one of its plantations.
steps.selling-2: Three plantations, but how many can sell? Your city wants two rice. Bali's rice has no ship near it. And the Sumatran's ship beside your city can carry two of yours now, thanks to Hull. So: two sales.
steps.sell-2: Tap your city for the first.
steps.sell-rest: For the second, tap Deliver: it sends whatever is left the cheapest way. When you care whose ships carry a good, tap a ship of the line you want instead.
steps.sold-2: Two rice sold, each on the ship beside your city. Your two plantations in Jawa Barat touch, so they make one group, and a good can leave from any coast of its group. 40 rupiah, less 10 in fees. Your Bali rice stays home: no ship reaches it.
steps.paid-expansion: You didn't sell everything, so there's no free growth. But a company that didn't sell out may still grow, if you pay: the good's price for each new area, 20 for rice, as many as your Expansion level. It comes from cash: this year's earnings can't be spent until next year. Next year you'll want your cash.
steps.others-sultan-pays: The Sultan runs Maluku spice. No ship there either, so nothing sells. But the Sultan pays 25 for a second spice area, ready for when ships arrive.
steps.growth-2: Phase seven. Your city got its two rice, but no spice. No city got any spice this year, so none grows. Every good grown anywhere counts, even one no ship can bring.
steps.year-3: Year three, and your earnings become cash. Look at what's left on offer: only shipping lines. Every company left is the same kind, so era A is over. Era B begins.
steps.others-sumatran-city-b: A new era starts with new cities, in the order of play, from everyone's era B card. The Sumatran's card. A city at home, in Sumatera Utara.
steps.your-card-b: Your era B card names Sumatera Barat, Kalimantan Selatan and Lampung.
steps.build-city-b: Build in Lampung: tap this area. It touches both of the Lampung line's seas, so your goods can reach it.
steps.others-sultan-city-b: The Sultan's card: Sumatera Utara is taken, so the city goes in Maluku. If none of a card's provinces has room, the card is thrown away and no city is built.
steps.era-b-companies: Then the era A companies nobody started are thrown out, and era B's come in. A company with no room left in its province to start is thrown out too. Remember the symbols beside each province's name? These are the ones that said B: Jawa Barat promised a shipping line in era B, and here it is. And the Lampung line may now have three ships.
steps.siap-saji: Phase three, and something new. From era B on, a rice company and a spice company may merge into siap saji, ready-cooked food, which sells for 35, more than either. Your rice and the Sumatran's spice would make three deeds, which is why you took Mergers to step three.
steps.siap-saji-how: It's an auction as before, and the two companies needn't be the same size, but every rice and spice good counts 25. Afterwards, half the goods are given up, rounded up, and the rest become siap saji.
steps.announce-ss: Tap one of your rice plantations.
steps.announce-ss-second: Then the Sumatran's spice, in Halmahera.
steps.ss-table: Four goods at 25: the bidding opens at 100, with raises of four. Three parts of the price would come to you, one to the Sumatran.
steps.others-pass-ss: The Sultan has a free slot, but can't afford to raise: a bid must be cash in hand. The Sumatran passes.
steps.give-up-why: It's yours, and 75 of your 100 comes straight back. Now half of the four goods must go: two. You choose, but only from the edges: a group of plantations may never be cut in two.
steps.give-up: Give up the spice in Halmahera: tap it.
steps.siap-saji-made: The two plantations left in Jawa Barat now grow siap saji. From now on, a siap saji company can only merge with another siap saji company.
steps.acquisitions-3: Phase four, with era B's companies. Your slot is full again; the others have room.
steps.others-sumatran-rubber: The Sumatran starts Sumatera Barat rubber.
steps.others-sultan-rubber: And the Sultan starts the rubber next door, in Riau. Look where it can't go: these areas touch the Sumatran's rubber. Two companies of the same good may never touch, so on the map you can always tell whose plantation is whose. It also means a plantation can wall in a rival, and keep it from growing your way. Then the Sultan passes.
steps.research-expansion: Take Expansion this time. Your company is about to sell everything it grows, and Expansion lets it grow two areas at a time. Tap the next step on the Expansion row.
steps.others-sumatran-ship-3: Phase six. The Lampung line adds its third ship, its new limit in era B.
steps.operate-ss: Run your siap saji: tap one of its plantations.
steps.sell-ss: Every city wants siap saji now, because it's being grown. Tap Deliver to sell it the cheapest way.
steps.ss-sold: Two siap saji at 35, one to each of your cities: 70, less 10 in fees. That's everything you had, so you grow for free, and with Expansion at two, by up to two areas.
steps.others-run-3: The others' plantations have no ships nearby, so nothing sells.
steps.growth-3: Phase seven. Cities now want siap saji, spice and rubber. No city got all three, so none grows. The more goods there are, the harder growing gets.
steps.ending: That's every rule but the last. The eras go on the same way: era C brings oil, the richest good, at 40 a barrel. When era C ends, at the start of a year, the game ends there. Everything earned in that last year's running of companies is doubled. Then the richest player, cash and Bank together, wins; a tie goes to whoever is earlier in the order of play.
steps.finish: Three years ago you had 100 rupiah and no company. Now you run the only siap saji company in Indonesia, with ships to carry it and cities to buy it. Read the symbols, watch the ships, and keep some cash for mergers. The game is yours.

hints.pick-company: Tap the Jawa Barat rice marker, off the coast of Jawa Barat.
hints.research-mergers: Tap the highlighted step on the Mergers row.
hints.sell: Tap your city in Jawa Barat.
hints.announce: Tap one of your rice plantations.
hints.announce-second: Tap the rice plantation in Bali.
hints.research-mergers-3: Tap the highlighted step on the Mergers row.
hints.operate-rice-2: Tap one of your rice plantations.
hints.sell-2: Tap your city in Jawa Barat.
hints.build-city-b: Tap the highlighted area in Lampung.
hints.announce-ss: Tap one of your rice plantations.
hints.announce-ss-second: Tap the spice plantation in Halmahera.
